newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MUM'S THE WORD FOR LAW-ABIDING AC MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MUM'S THE WORD FOR LAW-ABIDING AC MILAN.

text.p: Don't ask AC Milan why Dejan Savicevic won't be playing on Sunday.

The serie A champions, giving a strict reading to a new law on privacy which forbids divulging information on the health of individuals, say they can no longer make public news on the health of their players.
"Whether we like it or not, this law has been passed and everyone must respect it," team doctor Giovan Battista Monti was quoted as telling L'Unita daily.
"We consulted our club lawyer and the situation appeared quite clear. The new law prevents me as a doctor giving out any news on the health of the players.
"The club can only say which players took part in practice and which did not," he said.

While no other serie A clubs have shown signs of following the literal letter of the law -- which newspapers say is likely to be modified -- Milan did not hesitate to toe the line in their traditional pre-match statement on Friday.

"State of squad: (striker Marco) Simone, Savicevic and (defender Paolo) Coco did not work out and are unlikely to play against Reggiana," the statement said, without saying why the players did not train.
Surprised reporters were told to ask the players themselves if they were injured or not.
Asked what he thought of the new law, Savicevic said he quite liked it.

"But I think it's wrong to prevent a club from saying that a player is injured," said the former Belgrade Red Star player, adding that he was suffering from a thigh injury that would keep him out for a week.

"But I think the clubs should stop there, without specifying the kind of injury because otherwise the newspapers talk all week about 'Savicevic's bad right ankle' and as soon as I hit the pitch I take a kick right on my right ankle."
